features.description: Derive the rendered gate from the pending-gate fact the emit site already publishes and stop the renderer substituting the stage, so approval copy names the gate the supervisor actually paused on
steps: Read evidence/2026-08-13-live-false-gate-capture.md first: the emit site already publishes technical_metadata['pending_gates'] (2026-08-09-002 F005), so this feature is a renderer change only. Do not re-add emit-site gate metadata.

Reproduce the two false renders before changing anything: drive supervisor._emit_gate_paused_discord with (pending_gates=['pre_merge'], stage='general') and (pending_gates=['breaker:iteration_cap'], stage='upfront') against a spied notify_event.dispatch_event, and persist the rendered gate and exact_command

Make _gather_fields derive the gate format field from technical_metadata['pending_gates'], and remove the fallback to gate/subtype so an unknown gate renders as absent, matching the precedent already set by _reference_gate_stage

Define the multi-gate rendering rather than inheriting it: pending_gates is already a comma-joined string, so a naive substitution emits 'approve <plan> pre_merge, on_escalation', which is not runnable. Decide and document what a multi-gate pause prints.
Re-render the same two captured events and diff against the before evidence: gate must read pre_merge and breaker:iteration_cap respectively, while stage still reads general and upfront
Sweep the other emit sites for reliance on the removed alias and record any that lose a previously-rendered gate
features.acceptance: (1) Driving the real _emit_gate_paused_discord with pending_gates=['pre_merge'], stage='general' renders gate `pre_merge` and stage `general` as distinct values, and no rendered slot contains the string 'gate `general`'. (2) The same holds for pending_gates=['breaker:iteration_cap'], stage='upfront': no rendered slot contains 'upfront' as a gate. (3) The two call sites that pass a non-gate stage (supervisor.py:1316 'general' and supervisor.py:2021 'upfront') are both covered by a test, and the test names them so a future re-homing of the call is caught. (4) _gather_fields no longer falls back to subtype for the gate slot, and a gate-shaped event with no pending_gates metadata renders with the gate omitted rather than substituted. (5) A multi-gate pause with pending_gates of length 2 renders a documented, runnable-or-absent command — specifically it must not print a single approve command containing a comma. (6) The stage='pre_merge' site still renders exactly as it does today, proving the change did not regress the two already-correct call sites. (7) The full existing event_copy and messaging suites pass with no new failures against a same-scope baseline.

user_impact.summary: The approval prompt names the gate that is actually blocking, instead of repeating the stage name in its place.

features.description: Guarantee the rendered exact_command names the real pending gate, and add a standing invariant test that fails any renderable kind whose output names a gate absent from its source event
steps: Assert the exact_command for a gate-pause event ends in the real pending gate and is runnable as printed
Add an invariant test over every renderable kind: no rendered slot may name a gate that is not present in the source event's gate metadata
Confirm the invariant is not vacuous by mutating the gate slot and observing the test fail
Confirm the invariant would have caught the original defect by running it against the pre-F001 emit path
features.acceptance: (1) A test asserts the rendered exact_command for a gate pause on pre_merge is exactly 'dontpanic approve <plan_id> pre_merge'. (2) An invariant test iterates every renderable kind and fails if any rendered slot names a gate absent from the source event. (3) The invariant is proven non-vacuous: a deliberate mutation reintroducing the subtype-to-gate alias makes it fail, and that failure is captured as evidence. (4) The parametrized kind set is derived from the disposition table rather than hardcoded, and is asserted non-empty. (5) pytest passes for the new module and the full suite shows no new failures against a same-scope baseline.

user_impact.summary: The approve command shown at a gate can be pasted and will clear the gate it claims to clear.

features.description: Record on the README and CHANGELOG that the approve command names the gate the supervisor actually paused on
steps: If 2026-08-09-002 F010 already added a gates-in-product-terms line, extend that line rather than adding a second README section
State that the printed approve command names the pending gate and can be pasted
Add a root CHANGELOG entry for the operator-visible command fix
Do not restyle the README hook
features.acceptance: (1) README states that the approve command names the gate that is actually pending. (2) CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased or dated entry for this fix. (3) No second 'what is DontPanic' section is invented. (4) A reader can tell this is different from `dontpanic approve <plan> general`, the non-gate token the command used to print.

user_impact.summary: The landing page says the approve command you paste will clear the gate that is actually blocking.
